## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
In his analysis of the canonical *Cariyāpiṭaka* accounts in comparison with the *Jātaka* tales, Bareau documents the text's opening verses, where the Bodhisatta recalls his existence as Mahāgovinda and his practice of giving without regret for the sake of attaining complete Awakening [Bareau]. The tale's title also appears in Richard Morris's edition of the text, noting correspondences in title between *Jātaka* narratives and *Cariyāpiṭaka* stories [Morris 1882], and it is indexed in K. R. Norman's survey of Pali literature [Norman 1983].
Neither SuttaCentral nor DharmaNexus records any direct external parallels or text-reuse alignments for this short poetic narrative [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
